_**User (1970-01-01 00:00:00Z)**_

Let's make a new p5js sketch (in instance mode). The canvas will be a 600x600 square, and it will load a square image. The sketch will display the image at canvas size, then shrink it down to fit into a grid square (the square canvas can be dividied into a 10x10 grid of 60x60 squares). The shrinking will take 10 steps, and as the image shrinks from 600x600 at the canvas center, it will be drawn centered going towards the target grid square. Does this description make sense?

---

_**Agent**_

Yes, the description makes sense. Here's a step-by-step plan to create the p5.js sketch in instance mode:

1. Create a new p5.js sketch in instance mode.
2. Set up the canvas with a size of 600x600.
3. Load a square image.
4. Display the image at the canvas size (600x600) centered on the canvas.
5. Shrink the image in 10 steps to fit into a 60x60 grid square.
6. As the image shrinks, draw it centered and move it towards the target grid square.

Here's the code to achieve this:

```javascript
let sketch = function(p) {
  let img;
  let targetX = 300; // Center of the canvas
  let targetY = 300; // Center of the canvas
  let targetSize = 600; // Initial size of the image
  let step = 0; // Step counter

  p.preload = function() {
    img = p.loadImage('path/to/your/image.jpg'); // Load your image here
  };

  p.setup = function() {
    p.createCanvas(600, 600);
  };

  p.draw = function() {
    p.background(255);

    if (step < 10) {
      let size = p.lerp(600, 60, step / 10);
      let x = p.lerp(300, 30, step / 10);
      let y = p.lerp(300, 30, step / 10);
      p.image(img, x - size / 2, y - size / 2, size, size);
      step++;
    } else {
      p.image(img, 30, 30, 60, 60); // Final position in the top-left grid square
    }
  };
};

new p5(sketch);
```

Replace `'path/to/your/image.jpg'` with the actual path to your image file. This code will create a p5.js sketch that displays the image at the center of the canvas and shrinks it down to fit into the top-left grid square in 10 steps.

_**Agent**_

To modify the sketch to fill all the grid squares in sequence, we need to update the code to handle multiple grid squares and move the image to each square in sequence. Here's the updated code:

```javascript
let sketch = function(p) {
  let img;
  let targetSize = 600; // Initial size of the image
  let step = 0; // Step counter
  let gridX = 0; // Current grid column
  let gridY = 0; // Current grid row

  p.preload = function() {
    img = p.loadImage('images/mona.png'); // Load your image here
  };

  p.setup = function() {
    p.createCanvas(600, 600);
  };

  p.draw = function() {
    p.background(255);

    if (step < 10) {
      let size = p.lerp(600, 60, step / 10);
      let x = p.lerp(300, gridX * 60 + 30, step / 10);
      let y = p.lerp(300, gridY * 60 + 30, step / 10);
      p.image(img, x - size / 2, y - size / 2, size, size);
      step++;
    } else {
      p.image(img, gridX * 60, gridY * 60, 60, 60); // Final position in the current grid square
      step = 0; // Reset step counter
      gridX++; // Move to the next column
      if (gridX >= 10) {
        gridX = 0; // Reset column and move to the next row
        gridY++;
        if (gridY >= 10) {
          gridY = 0; // Reset row if all rows are filled
        }
      }
    }
  };
};

new p5(sketch);
```

This code will now fill all the grid squares in sequence, moving the image from one square to the next after shrinking it down to fit into the current grid square.

Sure, we can use a `PGraphics` object to hold the image of completed grid squares and paint that to the canvas before painting the shrinking image on top of it. Here's the updated code:

```javascript
let sketch = function(p) {
  let img;
  let pg;
  let targetSize = 600; // Initial size of the image
  let step = 0; // Step counter
  let gridX = 0; // Current grid column
  let gridY = 0; // Current grid row

  p.preload = function() {
    img = p.loadImage('images/mona.png'); // Load your image here
  };

  p.setup = function() {
    p.createCanvas(600, 600);
    pg = p.createGraphics(600, 600);
  };

  p.draw = function() {
    p.background(255);
    p.image(pg, 0, 0); // Draw the completed grid squares

    if (step < 10) {
      let size = p.lerp(600, 60, step / 10);
      let x = p.lerp(300, gridX * 60 + 30, step / 10);
      let y = p.lerp(300, gridY * 60 + 30, step / 10);
      p.image(img, x - size / 2, y - size / 2, size, size);
      step++;
    } else {
      pg.image(img, gridX * 60, gridY * 60, 60, 60); // Draw the final position in the current grid square to the PGraphics object
      step = 0; // Reset step counter
      gridX++; // Move to the next column
      if (gridX >= 10) {
        gridX = 0; // Reset column and move to the next row
        gridY++;
        if (gridY >= 10) {
          gridY = 0; // Reset row if all rows are filled
        }
      }
    }
  };
};

new p5(sketch);
```

This code will now use a `PGraphics` object to hold the image of completed grid squares, ensuring that they remain visible as the shrinking image is drawn on top of them.

_**Agent**_

Sure, let's extract the shrinking code into a separate function. Here's the updated code:

```javascript
let step = 0; // Step counter
let gridX = 0; // Current grid column
let gridY = 0; // Current grid row
const shrinkSteps = 20;
const gridCount = 5; // assuming a square, so really gridCount x gridCount
const targetSize = 600; // Initial size of the image
const tileSize = Math.floor(targetSize / gridCount);

let img;
let pg;

function shrinkImage(p) {
  let size = p.lerp(targetSize, tileSize, step / shrinkSteps);
  let x = p.lerp(targetSize / 2, gridX * tileSize + tileSize / 2, step / shrinkSteps);
  let y = p.lerp(targetSize / 2, gridY * tileSize + tileSize / 2, step / shrinkSteps);
  p.image(img, x - size / 2, y - size / 2, size, size);
}

let sketch = function(p) {
  p.preload = function() {
    img = p.loadImage('images/mona.png'); // Load your image here
  };

  p.setup = function() {
    p.createCanvas(targetSize, targetSize);
    pg = p.createGraphics(targetSize, targetSize);
  };

  p.draw = function() {
    p.background(255);
    p.image(pg, 0, 0); // Draw the completed grid squares

    if (step < shrinkSteps) {
      shrinkImage(p);
      step++;
    } else {
      pg.image(img, gridX * tileSize, gridY * tileSize, tileSize, tileSize); // Draw the final position in the current grid square to the PGraphics object
      step = 0; // Reset step counter
      gridX++; // Move to the next column
      if (gridX >= gridCount) {
        gridX = 0; // Reset column and move to the next row
        gridY++;
        if (gridY >= gridCount) {
          gridY = 0; // Reset row if all rows are filled
        }
      }
    }
  };
};

new p5(sketch);
```

The `shrinkImage` function now handles the shrinking and positioning of the image. This makes the code more modular and easier to manage.

_**User (1970-01-01 00:00:00Z)**_

Great! Now, can we make the tile order random, instead of sequential?

---

_**Agent**_

Sure, we can make the tile order random by shuffling the grid positions and then iterating through them. Here's the updated code:

```javascript
let step = 0; // Step counter
let gridIndex = 0; // Current grid index
const shrinkSteps = 20;
const gridCount = 5; // assuming a square, so really gridCount x gridCount
const targetSize = 600; // Initial size of the image
const tileSize = Math.floor(targetSize / gridCount);

let img;
let pg;
let gridPositions = [];

function shuffle(array) {
  for (let i = array.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
    const j = Math.floor(Math.random() * (i + 1));
    [array[i], array[j]] = [array[j], array[i]];
  }
}

function shrinkImage(p, gridX, gridY) {
  let size = p.lerp(targetSize, tileSize, step / shrinkSteps);
  let x = p.lerp(targetSize / 2, gridX * tileSize + tileSize / 2, step / shrinkSteps);
  let y = p.lerp(targetSize / 2, gridY * tileSize + tileSize / 2, step / shrinkSteps);
  p.image(img, x - size / 2, y - size / 2, size, size);
}

let sketch = function(p) {
  p.preload = function() {
    img = p.loadImage('images/mona.png'); // Load your image here
  };

  p.setup = function() {
    p.createCanvas(targetSize, targetSize);
    pg = p.createGraphics(targetSize, targetSize);

    // Initialize grid positions
    for (let y = 0; y < gridCount; y++) {
      for (let x = 0; x < gridCount; x++) {
        gridPositions.push({ x, y });
      }
    }

    // Shuffle grid positions
    shuffle(gridPositions);
  };

  p.draw = function() {
    p.background(255);
    p.image(pg, 0, 0); // Draw the completed grid squares

    if (step < shrinkSteps) {
      let { x: gridX, y: gridY } = gridPositions[gridIndex];
      shrinkImage(p, gridX, gridY);
      step++;
    } else {
      let { x: gridX, y: gridY } = gridPositions[gridIndex];
      pg.image(img, gridX * tileSize, gridY * tileSize, tileSize, tileSize); // Draw the final position in the current grid square to the PGraphics object
      step = 0; // Reset step counter
      gridIndex++; // Move to the next grid position
      if (gridIndex >= gridPositions.length) {
        gridIndex = 0; // Reset index if all positions are filled
      }
    }
  };
};

new p5(sketch);
```

This code will now fill the grid squares in a random order by shuffling the grid positions and iterating through them.

_**Agent**_

Yes, you can avoid repetition by using a flag to check if the grid is complete and then handle the drawing accordingly. Here's the updated code:

```javascript
let step = 0; // Step counter
let gridIndex = 0; // Current grid index
const shrinkSteps = 20;
const gridCount = 5; // assuming a square, so really gridCount x gridCount
const targetSize = 600; // Initial size of the image
const tileSize = Math.floor(targetSize / gridCount);

let img;
let pg;
let gridPositions = [];
let gridComplete = false;

function shuffle(array) {
  for (let i = array.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
    const j = Math.floor(Math.random() * (i + 1));
    [array[i], array[j]] = [array[j], array[i]];
  }
}

function shrinkImage(p, gridX, gridY) {
  let size = p.lerp(targetSize, tileSize, step / shrinkSteps);
  let x = p.lerp(targetSize / 2, gridX * tileSize + tileSize / 2, step / shrinkSteps);
  let y = p.lerp(targetSize / 2, gridY * tileSize + tileSize / 2, step / shrinkSteps);
  p.image(img, x - size / 2, y - size / 2, size, size);
}

let sketch = function(p) {
  p.preload = function() {
    img = p.loadImage('images/mona.png'); // Load your image here
  };

  p.setup = function() {
    p.createCanvas(targetSize, targetSize);
    pg = p.createGraphics(targetSize, targetSize);

    // Initialize grid positions
    for (let y = 0; y < gridCount; y++) {
      for (let x = 0; x < gridCount; x++) {
        gridPositions.push({ x, y });
      }
    }

    // Shuffle grid positions
    shuffle(gridPositions);
  };

  p.draw = function() {
    p.background(255);
    p.image(pg, 0, 0); // Draw the completed grid squares

    if (!gridComplete) {
      if (step < shrinkSteps) {
        let { x: gridX, y: gridY } = gridPositions[gridIndex];
        shrinkImage(p, gridX, gridY);
        step++;
      } else {
        let { x: gridX, y: gridY } = gridPositions[gridIndex];
        pg.image(img, gridX * tileSize, gridY * tileSize, tileSize, tileSize); // Draw the final position in the current grid square to the PGraphics object
        step = 0; // Reset step counter
        gridIndex++; // Move to the next grid position
        if (gridIndex >= gridPositions.length) {
          gridComplete = true; // Mark the grid as complete
          p.noLoop(); // Stop the draw loop
        }
      }
    }
  };
};

new p5(sketch);
```

In this version, a `gridComplete` flag is used to check if the grid is complete. When the grid is complete, the [`p.noLoop()`](command:_github.copilot.openSymbolFromReferences?%5B%22%22%2C%5B%7B%22uri%22%3A%7B%22scheme%22%3A%22file%22%2C%22authority%22%3A%22%22%2C%22path%22%3A%22%2FUsers%2Fmichaelpaulukonis%2Fprojects%2Fmy-sketches%2Ftemp%2Fde.zoom.grid.js%22%2C%22query%22%3A%22%22%2C%22fragment%22%3A%22%22%7D%2C%22pos%22%3A%7B%22line%22%3A31%2C%22character%22%3A4%7D%7D%5D%2C%22b39cef77-a8ae-47d4-925d-d3997bef3464%22%5D "Go to definition") function is called to stop the draw loop, and the completed grid is drawn once in the [`p.draw`](command:_github.copilot.openSymbolFromReferences?%5B%22%22%2C%5B%7B%22uri%22%3A%7B%22scheme%22%3A%22file%22%2C%22authority%22%3A%22%22%2C%22path%22%3A%22%2FUsers%2Fmichaelpaulukonis%2Fprojects%2Fmy-sketches%2Ftemp%2Fde.zoom.grid.js%22%2C%22query%22%3A%22%22%2C%22fragment%22%3A%22%22%7D%2C%22pos%22%3A%7B%22line%22%3A31%2C%22character%22%3A4%7D%7D%5D%2C%22b39cef77-a8ae-47d4-925d-d3997bef3464%22%5D "Go to definition") function. Thank you. How can we change the shrinking algorithm from a smooth lerp to something that starts out slowly and increases the fewer steps remain?

---

_**Agent**_

To change the shrinking algorithm from a smooth linear interpolation (`lerp`) to one that starts out slowly and increases speed as fewer steps remain, we can use an easing function. One common easing function is the quadratic easing function.

Here's how you can modify the code to use a quadratic easing function:

```javascript
let step = 0; // Step counter
let gridIndex = 0; // Current grid index
const shrinkSteps = 20;
const gridCount = 5; // assuming a square, so really gridCount x gridCount
const targetSize = 600; // Initial size of the image
const tileSize = Math.floor(targetSize / gridCount);

let img;
let pg;
let gridPositions = [];
let gridComplete = false;

function shuffle(array) {
  for (let i = array.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
    const j = Math.floor(Math.random() * (i + 1));
    [array[i], array[j]] = [array[j], array[i]];
  }
}

function easeInQuad(t) {
  return t * t;
}

function shrinkImage(p, gridX, gridY) {
  let t = step / shrinkSteps;
  let easedT = easeInQuad(t);
  let size = p.lerp(targetSize, tileSize, easedT);
  let x = p.lerp(targetSize / 2, gridX * tileSize + tileSize / 2, easedT);
  let y = p.lerp(targetSize / 2, gridY * tileSize + tileSize / 2, easedT);
  p.image(img, x - size / 2, y - size / 2, size, size);
}

let sketch = function(p) {
  p.preload = function() {
    img = p.loadImage('images/mona.png'); // Load your image here
  };

  p.setup = function() {
    p.createCanvas(targetSize, targetSize);
    pg = p.createGraphics(targetSize, targetSize);

    // Initialize grid positions
    for (let y = 0; y < gridCount; y++) {
      for (let x = 0; x < gridCount; x++) {
        gridPositions.push({ x, y });
      }
    }

    // Shuffle grid positions
    shuffle(gridPositions);
  };

  p.draw = function() {
    p.background(255);
    p.image(pg, 0, 0); // Draw the completed grid squares

    if (!gridComplete) {
      if (step < shrinkSteps) {
        let { x: gridX, y: gridY } = gridPositions[gridIndex];
        shrinkImage(p, gridX, gridY);
        step++;
      } else {
        let { x: gridX, y: gridY } = gridPositions[gridIndex];
        pg.image(img, gridX * tileSize, gridY * tileSize, tileSize, tileSize); // Draw the final position in the current grid square to the PGraphics object
        step = 0; // Reset step counter
        gridIndex++; // Move to the next grid position
        if (gridIndex >= gridPositions.length) {
          gridComplete = true; // Mark the grid as complete
          p.noLoop(); // Stop the draw loop
        }
      }
    }
  };
};

new p5(sketch);
```

In this version, the `easeInQuad` function is used to calculate the eased time `easedT`, which is then used in the [`p.lerp`](command:_github.copilot.openSymbolFromReferences?%5B%22%22%2C%5B%7B%22uri%22%3A%7B%22scheme%22%3A%22file%22%2C%22authority%22%3A%22%22%2C%22path%22%3A%22%2FUsers%2Fmichaelpaulukonis%2Fprojects%2Fmy-sketches%2Ftemp%2Fde.zoom.grid.js%22%2C%22query%22%3A%22%22%2C%22fragment%22%3A%22%22%7D%2C%22pos%22%3A%7B%22line%22%3A31%2C%22character%22%3A4%7D%7D%5D%2C%224294c80a-8252-4408-ba23-33b0425cde05%22%5D "Go to definition") function to create the effect of starting slowly and increasing speed as fewer steps remain.

```javascript
p.setup = function() {
  p.createCanvas(targetSize, targetSize);
  pg = p.createGraphics(targetSize, targetSize);

  // Initialize grid positions
  for (let y = 0; y < gridCount; y++) {
    for (let x = 0; x < gridCount; x++) {
      gridPositions.push({ x, y });
    }
  }

  shuffle(gridPositions);
};

p.draw = function() {
  p.background(255);
  p.image(pg, 0, 0); // Draw the completed grid squares

    let { x: gridX, y: gridY } = gridPositions[gridIndex];

    step++;
  } else {
    let { x: gridX, y: gridY } = gridPositions[gridIndex];

    step = 0; // Reset step counter

      gridIndex = 0; // Reset index if all positions are filled
    }
  }
};

function shrinkImage(p, gridX, gridY) {
  let t = step / shrinkSteps;
  let easedT = easeInQuad(t);
  let size = p.lerp(targetSize, tileSize, easedT);
  let x = p.lerp(targetSize / 2, gridX * tileSize + tileSize / 2, easedT);
  let y = p.lerp(targetSize / 2, gridY * tileSize + tileSize / 2, easedT);

  // Set transparency for the first few steps
  let alpha = p.lerp(255, 0, t);
  p.tint(255, alpha);

  p.image(img, x - size / 2, y - size / 2, size, size);

  // Reset tint to default
  p.noTint();
}

function easeInQuad(t) {
  return t * t;
}

In this version, the [`shrinkImage`](command:_github.copilot.openSymbolFromReferences?%5B%22%22%2C%5B%7B%22uri%22%3A%7B%22scheme%22%3A%22file%22%2C%22authority%22%3A%22%22%2C%22path%22%3A%22%2FUsers%2Fmichaelpaulukonis%2Fprojects%2Fmy-sketches%2Ftemp%2Fde.zoom.grid.js%22%2C%22query%22%3A%22%22%2C%22fragment%22%3A%22%22%7D%2C%22pos%22%3A%7B%22line%22%3A56%2C%22character%22%3A6%7D%7D%5D%2C%22ac5fd863-e2ce-4e91-9e2e-50cd44a91676%22%5D "Go to definition") function uses the [`p.tint`](command:_github.copilot.openSymbolFromReferences?%5B%22%22%2C%5B%7B%22uri%22%3A%7B%22scheme%22%3A%22file%22%2C%22authority%22%3A%22%22%2C%22path%22%3A%22%2FUsers%2Fmichaelpaulukonis%2Fprojects%2Fmy-sketches%2Ftemp%2Fde.zoom.grid.js%22%2C%22query%22%3A%22%22%2C%22fragment%22%3A%22%22%7D%2C%22pos%22%3A%7B%22line%22%3A36%2C%22character%22%3A2%7D%7D%5D%2C%22ac5fd863-e2ce-4e91-9e2e-50cd44a91676%22%5D "Go to definition") function to set the transparency of the image based on the current step. ```javascript
let step = 0; // Step counter
let gridIndex = 0; // Current grid index
const initialShrinkSteps = 20;
const minShrinkSteps = 5;
const gridCount = 5; // assuming a square, so really gridCount x gridCount
const targetSize = 600; // Initial size of the image
const tileSize = Math.floor(targetSize / gridCount);

let img;
let pg;
let gridPositions = [];
let gridComplete = false;

function easeInOutQuad(t) {
  return t < 0.5 ? 2 * t * t : -1 + (4 - 2 * t) * t;
}

function getShrinkSteps(gridIndex, totalGrids) {
  let t = gridIndex / totalGrids;
  let easedT = easeInOutQuad(t);
  return Math.floor(p.lerp(initialShrinkSteps, minShrinkSteps, easedT));
}

function shrinkImage(p, gridX, gridY, shrinkSteps) {
  let t = step / shrinkSteps;
  let easedT = easeInQuad(t);
  let size = p.lerp(targetSize, tileSize, easedT);
  let x = p.lerp(targetSize / 2, gridX * tileSize + tileSize / 2, easedT);
  let y = p.lerp(targetSize / 2, gridY * tileSize + tileSize / 2, easedT);

  // Set transparency for the first few steps
  let alpha = p.lerp(255, 0, t);
  p.tint(255, alpha);

  p.image(img, x - size / 2, y - size / 2, size, size);

  // Reset tint to default
  p.noTint();
}

let sketch = function(p) {
  p.preload = function() {
    img = p.loadImage('images/mona.png'); // Load your image here
  };

  p.setup = function() {
    p.createCanvas(targetSize, targetSize);
    pg = p.createGraphics(targetSize, targetSize);

    // Initialize grid positions
    for (let y = 0; y < gridCount; y++) {
      for (let x = 0; x < gridCount; x++) {
        gridPositions.push({ x, y });
      }
    }

    gridPositions = p.shuffle(gridPositions);
  };

  p.draw = function() {
    p.background(255);
    p.image(pg, 0, 0); // Draw the completed grid squares

    if (step < shrinkSteps) {
      let { x: gridX, y: gridY } = gridPositions[gridIndex];
      let shrinkSteps = getShrinkSteps(gridIndex, gridPositions.length);
      shrinkImage(p, gridX, gridY, shrinkSteps);
      step++;
    } else {
      let { x: gridX, y: gridY } = gridPositions[gridIndex];
      pg.image(img, gridX * tileSize, gridY * tileSize, tileSize, tileSize); // Draw the final position in the current grid square to the PGraphics object
      p.image(pg, 0, 0);

      step = 0; // Reset step counter
      gridIndex++; // Move to the next grid position
      if (gridIndex >= gridPositions.length) {
        p.image(pg, 0, 0);
        p.noLoop();
        gridIndex = 0; // Reset index if all positions are filled
      }
    }
  };
};

new p5(sketch);
```

In this version, the `getShrinkSteps` function calculates the number of shrinking steps dynamically based on the current grid index and the total number of grids. The `easeInOutQuad` function is used to create a non-linear easing effect, making the shrinking steps start slow and speed up as fewer steps remain. The [`shrinkImage`](command:_github.copilot.openSymbolFromReferences?%5B%22%22%2C%5B%7B%22uri%22%3A%7B%22scheme%22%3A%22file%22%2C%22authority%22%3A%22%22%2C%22path%22%3A%22%2FUsers%2Fmichaelpaulukonis%2Fprojects%2Fmy-sketches%2Ftemp%2Fde.zoom.grid.js%22%2C%22query%22%3A%22%22%2C%22fragment%22%3A%22%22%7D%2C%22pos%22%3A%7B%22line%22%3A57%2C%22character%22%3A6%7D%7D%5D%2C%22db2c6820-4aa3-4964-9783-22c55503ef65%22%5D "Go to definition") function now takes [`shrinkSteps`](command:_github.copilot.openSymbolFromReferences?%5B%22%22%2C%5B%7B%22uri%22%3A%7B%22scheme%22%3A%22file%22%2C%22authority%22%3A%22%22%2C%22path%22%3A%22%2FUsers%2Fmichaelpaulukonis%2Fprojects%2Fmy-sketches%2Ftemp%2Fde.zoom.grid.js%22%2C%22query%22%3A%22%22%2C%22fragment%22%3A%22%22%7D%2C%22pos%22%3A%7B%22line%22%3A55%2C%22character%22%3A15%7D%7D%5D%2C%22db2c6820-4aa3-4964-9783-22c55503ef65%22%5D "Go to definition") as a parameter to adjust the shrinking speed accordingly.
